title: NITI Aayog SDG India Index 2023-24: Sustainable Development Goals Progress Report
extracted_text: The SDG India Index 2023-24 computes composite scores for all states and union territories of India across 16 Sustainable Development Goals. India's overall composite SDG score has improved significantly from 57 in 2018 to 66 in 2020-21, and further to 74 in 2023-24. This progress highlights targeted government interventions in multidimensional poverty reduction, sanitation, clean water access, and renewable energy adoption. Among the states, Kerala and Uttarakhand emerged as top performers with identical composite scores of 79, followed closely by Tamil Nadu with a score of 78. Goal 1 (No Poverty) recorded the highest state-level increase, with 32 states and union territories advancing into the 'Front Runner' category with scores between 65 and 99. In addition, Goal 13 (Climate Action) demonstrated substantial momentum, driven by national solar expansion and disaster management protocols. However, disparities in gender equality (Goal 5) and industry innovation (Goal 9) persist in select eastern states, requiring coordinated inter-ministerial allocation in the upcoming fiscal planning cycle.
gold_key_facts: India's composite SDG score improved from 57 in 2018 to 74 in 2023-24.
Kerala and Uttarakhand achieved the top rank with composite scores of 79.
32 states and union territories entered the Front Runner category for Goal 1.
Tamil Nadu secured the third position with a score of 78.
Gender equality and industry innovation persist as key development challenges.

reference_outputs.EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY: The SDG India Index 2023-24 by NITI Aayog documents steady nationwide advancement across 16 Sustainable Development Goals, with the composite national score rising from 57 in 2018 to 74 in 2023-24. Key findings demonstrate that Kerala and Uttarakhand lead all states with composite scores of 79, followed by Tamil Nadu at 78. Substantial progress was recorded in Goal 1 (No Poverty), where 32 states achieved 'Front Runner' status. Major implications demand targeted capital allocation toward persistent regional lags in gender equality (Goal 5) and industrial innovation (Goal 9). Senior management should prioritize inter-ministerial resource deployment in lagging eastern states.

title: National Green Hydrogen Mission: Strategic Transition and Production Mandate
publisher: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), Govt of India
extracted_text: The Union Cabinet approved the National Green Hydrogen Mission with an initial outlay of Rs. 19,744 crore. The overarching objective is to make India a global hub for the production, utilization, and export of Green Hydrogen and its derivatives. By 2030, the mission targets building a domestic green hydrogen production capacity of at least 5 Million Metric Tonnes (MMT) per annum, supported by an addition of 125 GW of associated renewable energy capacity across the country. The mission is estimated to bring over Rs. 8 lakh crore in total investments and create over 6 lakh high-skilled green jobs by 2030. Furthermore, this strategic shift is projected to avert nearly 50 MMT of annual greenhouse gas emissions and reduce fossil fuel import expenditure by Rs. 1 lakh crore cumulatively. Two dedicated financial incentive mechanisms under the Strategic Interventions for Green Hydrogen Transition (SIGHT) program have been established: Component A focuses on domestic manufacturing of electrolyzers with an allocation of Rs. 4,440 crore, and Component B supports green hydrogen production with Rs. 13,050 crore.

Key financial mechanisms include the SIGHT program allocating Rs. 4,440 crore for electrolyzer manufacturing and Rs. 13,050 crore for green hydrogen production. Strategic implications include Rs. 1 lakh crore in fossil fuel import savings, 6 lakh skilled jobs, and 50 MMT annual emissions abatement. title: NITI Aayog Health Index 2024: State Performance on Health Outcomes
extracted_text: The NITI Aayog Health Index 2024 ranks states and union territories on 24 key health indicators spanning health outcomes, governance and information, and key inputs and processes. Kerala continues to dominate the overall rankings with a score of 82.2, followed by Tamil Nadu at 72.4 and Punjab at 69.9. The index reveals that 14 states improved their incremental performance between the base year (2019-20) and reference year (2021-22). Notably, Uttar Pradesh showed the highest incremental improvement of 7.6 points, driven by gains in institutional deliveries, immunization coverage, and functional health and wellness centers. However, the report flags persistent gaps in the density of medical officers at primary health centers, with a national average of only 0.6 medical officers per 10,000 population against the IPHS norm of 1.0. Neonatal mortality rate (NMR) ranges from a low of 4 per 1,000 live births in Kerala to a high of 28 in Madhya Pradesh. The full immunization coverage stands at 76.4% nationally, with 8 states achieving over 90% coverage.

Fourteen states improved incrementally, with Uttar Pradesh gaining 7.6 points through better institutional deliveries and immunization. title: School Education Quality Index (SEQI) 2023: State Rankings and Learning Outcomes
extracted_text: The School Education Quality Index 2023 assesses states and union territories on 30 indicators across learning outcomes, access, infrastructure, and equity. Kerala retains the top position among large states with a score of 76.6%, followed by Maharashtra at 74.6% and Punjab at 73.6%. Among smaller states, Goa leads at 80.2% and Mizoram at 75.8%. The index reveals that the national average learning outcome score for Class 5 language is 56.4% and for mathematics is 47.2%. Only 6 states have Class 5 math scores above 60%. The pupil-teacher ratio at the national level stands at 26:1, with 14 states exceeding the RTE norm of 30:1. Digital infrastructure remains a challenge: only 41.3% of government schools have functional computers, and 24.5% have internet connectivity. The gender parity index for secondary enrollment has improved to 1.02 nationally.

title: National Health Mission Annual Report 2023-24: Universal Health Coverage Progress
publisher: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW), Govt of India
extracted_text: The National Health Mission Annual Report 2023-24 documents India's progress toward Universal Health Coverage. Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) has provided 5.5 crore hospital admissions worth Rs. 70,000 crore since inception. The scheme covers 12 crore families (approx. 55 crore beneficiaries) with Rs. 5 lakh annual health cover per family. Under the Health and Wellness Centers initiative, 1.6 lakh centers have been operationalized against a target of 1.5 lakh, providing comprehensive primary care including NCD screening, maternal health, and teleconsultation. The National Digital Health Mission (ABDM) has created 50 crore Ayushman Bharat Health Accounts (ABHA), with 35 crore linked health records. Maternal Mortality Ratio declined from 130 per 100,000 live births in 2014-16 to 97 in 2018-20. Infant Mortality Rate reduced from 39 in 2014 to 28 in 2020. The doctor-population ratio improved to 1:834 against WHO norm of 1:1000.

title: World Bank India Development Update 2024: Growth, Resilience, and Reforms
extracted_text: The World Bank India Development Update 2024 projects India's GDP growth at 7.5% for FY2024-25, moderating to 6.7% in FY2025-26. The growth momentum is driven by robust domestic demand, continued public investment in infrastructure, and a rebound in private consumption. However, the report highlights downside risks from global uncertainty, geopolitical tensions, and potential monetary tightening in advanced economies. The current account deficit narrowed to 1.2% of GDP in FY2023-24 from 2.0% in the previous year, supported by strong services exports and remittances. Inflation has moderated to 5.4% in FY2023-24 from 6.7% in FY2022-23, within the RBI's target band. The fiscal deficit target of 5.1% of GDP for FY2024-25 is on track, with capital expenditure increasing to 3.4% of GDP. The report emphasizes the need for continued structural reforms in land, labor, and financial markets to sustain high growth.

title: WHO Global Air Quality Guidelines 2024: India Country Profile
extracted_text: The WHO Global Air Quality Guidelines 2024 country profile for India indicates that 99% of the population lives in areas exceeding WHO PM2.5 guidelines. Annual mean PM2.5 concentration in India is estimated at 58 µg/m³ against the WHO guideline of 5 µg/m³. Delhi records the highest annual average at 98 µg/m³, followed by Patna at 82 µg/m³ and Gwalior at 76 µg/m³. Air pollution contributes to an estimated 1.67 million premature deaths annually in India, accounting for 17.8% of all deaths. The economic cost of air pollution is estimated at 1.36% of GDP, approximately Rs. 3 lakh crore. The National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) targets 40% reduction in PM10 by 2025-26 from 2017 levels across 131 non-attainment cities. As of 2024, 95 cities have shown improvement in PM10 concentrations.

title: India Digital Economy Report 2024: Measuring the New Economy
extracted_text: The India Digital Economy Report 2024 estimates the digital economy's contribution at 11.7% of GDP in 2022-23, valued at approximately Rs. 31.6 lakh crore. This is projected to reach 20% of GDP by 2029-30. The core digital sector (ICT, digital platforms, e-commerce) contributes 6.3% of GDP. Digital payments volume surged to 13,462 crore transactions in FY2023-24, a 56% year-on-year increase, with UPI accounting for 80% of digital payment volume. The Unified Payments Interface processed Rs. 199 lakh crore in transaction value. Broadband subscribers reached 91 crore, with wireless broadband at 87 crore. Internet penetration stands at 55% nationally, with rural at 37% and urban at 71%. The report identifies 3.4 crore workers in the digital economy, expected to double by 2030.
